title: Efficiency hierarchy: LCPE, RARS, CSR scheduler, HCAR classifier

scope.objective: Implement the four-mechanism efficiency hierarchy: change envelopes with causality and resolution-aware quantised invalidation (LCPE), deterministic projection fidelity with hysteresis (RARS), topology-aware spatial scheduling with work stealing (CSR), and heterogeneous core classification with energy/deadline allocation (HCAR).
exclusions: tile-parallel raster execution (CSR scheduler contract only; backends are Wave-2c)
cgroup/affinity syscalls (HCAR is the classification contract)

implementation_record.notes: All four crates std-only and deterministic. LCPE: events rejected by default; quantisation conservative; persistence masks block forbidden dirty regions; cost model with union-first commit policy. RARS: n≈sqrt(1/eps) subdivision, raster scale from relative 4K area, temporal policy independent of spatial size, accessibility text protection. CSR: disjoint+complete territory partitioning proven by test, quad-corner worker mapping, greedy stealing from largest queue. HCAR: deadline-feasibility-first then energy-minimal, critical-path promotion, homogeneous degrade, migration residency seeded on first observation.

results.unit_tests: 210 passed, 0 failed (30 suites; +29 across the four new crates)
results.lcpe_live: presses produce quantised local damage decisions; cost model switches to full-frame for large unions
results.rars_live: glyph_px=4 (protected text), subdivisions=2, quality=balanced at 3.28% of 4K

notable_findings.union_bug: The cost-model union seeded from PixelRect::default() dragged the origin to (0,0), inflating small dirty regions to full-frame cost — caught by the small-dirty-region test.
notable_findings.residency_seed_bug: Both hysteresis wrappers (RARS, HCAR) returned the incoming class immediately before residency was seeded; fixed by seeding on first observation — the RARS test suite's implicit default-0 semantics were updated to the corrected behaviour.
